prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, in which magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms made possible fractional uncertainties at the 10^-18 level.

statement.case_for: I move my preferred configuration from B012 to B029. The chair asked what principle selects three individuals from ATLAS and CMS, and who made the decisive individual contribution. After reading all eight statements I cannot answer that honestly. My own round-1 text conceded that spokespersons at the time of discovery, detector pioneers and accelerator leaders have comparable claims, and five colleagues raised the same point independently. A prize that has to say the Higgs was discovered by three founders and leaders, when the discovery was made by two collaborations of thousands, would put a statement into the citation that I cannot defend. The science of B012 is not in doubt, and I still think the experimental side is overdue, but a Nobel citation needs names that the committee can stand behind. B029 meets that test. It is a well-bounded invention: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice removes Doppler and recoil shifts and the light shift while keeping many atoms, and Ye's group took strontium lattice clocks to 10^-18 and into many-body clock physics. The performance has been reproduced and intercompared at several independent laboratories, and every member who proposed laureates gave the same two names. On the overlap question the chair raised, I think the lattice clock is a separate step. The 2005 prize honoured the comb as a way to count optical cycles, and the 2012 prize honoured control and readout of single trapped quantum systems. The lattice clock combines a different idea, interrogating a large ensemble of neutral atoms at a magic wavelength, with that toolkit, and the resulting systematic and statistical performance is not something either earlier citation covers. I would build the citation on the invention and the demonstrated 10^-18 performance, and leave the redefinition of the second and any future test of constants out of the merit.
statement.case_against: The reservation I take most seriously is the one all six supporters state. The comb and ion-control prizes sit directly under this work, the lattice clocks read out through a comb, and Al+ ion clocks competed on accuracy, so a sceptic can call B029 a refinement of an honoured programme rather than a new discovery about nature. As a theorist I also notice that this is a metrological achievement more than a discovery, and I gave that distinction weight in round 1. I have not changed my view that an actual discovery is worth more than a better instrument, but I now see that the committee has no discovery candidate on this list with a clean credit, and I will not let that preference override a sound attribution. Two further weaknesses remain. Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat, Hinkley, Bloom, Schiller and the Yb and Al+ groups reached comparable accuracy and are outside the two names, so the citation should name the concept and its realisation, not a record that several groups share. And I cannot judge the metrological details at the level of Lindroth or Kroll, so I rely on their reading of where the lattice idea ends and the stabilised lasers and cavities begin.

responses.point: The Higgs trio are founders and leaders of two collaborations of several thousand people, and spokespersons, analysis conveners and accelerator and detector pioneers have comparable claims, so B012 can stay a candidate only if the committee agrees a defensible rationale for the three names.
responses.response: You and I share the experimental-discovery instinct, and you put the difficulty more sharply than I had. As chair you asked me to state who made the decisive individual contribution and why spokespersons at the time and accelerator leaders are not credited. I cannot supply that argument. The roles of Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee as founders are real, but they are founding and construction roles, and the discovery analysis and the announcement belong to many others. I therefore do not carry B012 forward as my preferred part. I keep it as an alternative in case the committee finds a principled rule for crediting the experiments. You also ask the committee to test B029 as hard as any other case. I have tried, and the overlap with 2005 and 2012 is the real issue. I think it is answered by the neutral many-atom magic-wavelength scheme, but I do not think it is a trivial objection. I also hold that your B013 and B037 should not be reopened this year. The credit gaps your colleagues name for B013 (van Paradijs and the optical identification teams) and the single-name problem for B037 are real.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks have a clear originating idea in magic-wavelength trapping, are reproduced by independent laboratories, and the citation can add new tests of fundamental physics and a path to redefining the second.
responses.response: I agreed with your attribution argument in round 1 and now accept your conclusion on B029. I do not follow you on the wording. I would leave out the path to redefining the second and the new tests of fundamental physics. The redefinition has not happened, nobody has yet found a variation of a constant with these clocks, and a Nobel citation should rest on what has been demonstrated. Writing prospects into the citation also invites the objection that the committee is rewarding a roadmap. On your Hall-laboratory stay, I see a disclosure and not a recusal ground. You claim no collaboration, supervision or shared funding with Ye or Katori, and Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce reach B029 independently. My own position does not depend on yours.

responses.point: Dynamical mean-field theory (B035) is the strongest case on originality, durability and breadth, while Eriksson accepts that Metzner's omission is a real gap and that B031 is the mechanism-unsettled alternative.
responses.response: As a theorist I respect the conceptual weight of the infinite-dimension limit and the impurity mapping, and I understand why you rank it first. Where I stand is close to Johansson, Lindroth and Mehlig on the credit. Metzner's role in the limit, and Mueller-Hartmann, Jarrell and Rozenberg on the solution side, cannot be resolved by rewording a three-name citation without making it vague. I take your remark that B029 is now ranked too low by you as a real change of mind, and not as a counting argument, and I treat it that way. On B031 we agree that the origin of superconductivity and the correlated states is unsettled and that Cao and Fatemi are outside the credited set. That keeps it in my alternatives and not first.

responses.point: The overlap with Hall and Hansch (2005) and Wineland (2012) is the strongest reservation, and a sceptic could call the lattice clock a refinement of an honoured programme, so B018 should be weighed only after the Wineland overlap is settled.
responses.response: I agree that the overlap objection cannot be waved away, and I think it applies much more heavily to B018 than to B029. Cirac and Zoller's proposal, and Blatt's realisations, sit directly on Wineland's prize for control of individual trapped ions, and the remaining increment, quantum computation as an application, is still unfolding while platforms compete. For the lattice clock the 2012 work is a sibling, since it concerns a single ion in a Paul trap, and the magic-wavelength scheme with many neutral atoms is a different physical route to the same kind of clock. That is why I place B029 ahead of B018 and keep B018 out of my alternatives.

responses.point: Lattice clocks should not wait for the redefinition of the second, since waiting for a metrological decision is not a scientific criterion, and B031 is a good fallback because the prediction preceded the measurement.
responses.response: I agree that waiting for the redefinition is not a scientific criterion and that the citation should not depend on it. On B031 I agree that the theory preceded the experiment, which is unusual and speaks for the case. My reservation is about maturity and credit, not priority: the pairing mechanism is still debated, and the early experimental co-authors fall outside the three names. If B029 did not hold, I would still put B031 ahead of the others, but I would want the committee to say clearly how it treats Cao and Fatemi.

uncertainties: Whether the lattice clock is distinct enough from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. I think so, but I judge it as a theorist and I rely on Kroll's and Lindroth's reading of the metrology.

Whether the credited pair should be Katori and Ye alone, given Lemonde, Ludlow, Lisdat, Hinkley and the Yb and Al+ ion-clock groups. A change to the two-name set would not change my preferred configuration, but it would change how confident I am in the attribution.

Whether B012 would be defensible with a principled rule for naming individuals. I rely on general knowledge of founding roles and have not verified them in detail, and I could be wrong that no such rule exists.
Whether magic-angle graphene (B031) has matured enough, given the open question of the superconducting mechanism and the position of Cao and Fatemi.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my provided profile, and I have not changed this since round 1. My documented connections are my PhD supervisor David Gross, early mentor Hector Rubinstein, frequent co-author Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theoretical-physics group. None of these is a credited name or an apparent collaborator of Katori, Ye or the other shortlisted candidates. I have no link to the clock community. I take Kroll's Hall-laboratory disclosure as a disclosure to be recorded, not a ground for exclusion.
